newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures surge with all months limit-up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures surge with all months limit-up.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed sharply higher on Wednesday, with all months rising by their 400-yen limit on heavy buying by local investors, traders said.
The benchmark July 1998 ended up 400 yen at 14,410 yen per tonne. Estimated volume was 98,485 lots.

The yen's fall against the dollar and the rally in CBOT corn futures overnight encouraged investors to buy, traders said. "Everybody rushed to buy from the opening. The bullish mood remained throughout the day," a brokerage trader said.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.60-1/2 per bushel at 0820 GMT, against $2.58 at Tuesday's close.
The spot August CBOT soybean futures contract on the overnight trading system was at $7.67 per bushel at 0820 GMT, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
